Maya (docs): Quick ping — I'm updating private/install.md to clarify proxy + VPC networking for air-gapped installs. A customer hit a problem where the installer tried to pull images but egress is only allowed via an HTTP proxy and SNAT is blocked. What do we recommend? NAT gateway vs explicit HTTP proxy? @Liam

Liam (infra): +1 this is messy. Recommend documenting both: 1) prefer HTTP proxy env vars for egress to registries/CDNs; 2) fallback with NAT/SNAT for non-proxyable protocols (some registries/catalogs), with clear notes about route tables and costs. Also call out AWS NAT gateway billing.

Samir (eng): For the installer specifically, we added offline.proxy in v0.9.2 — set HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY in the systemd unit that runs the installer. Example snippet for systemd:
```bash
[Service]
Environment="HTTP_PROXY=http://10.0.0.5:3128" "HTTPS_PROXY=http://10.0.0.5:3128" "NO_PROXY=169.254.169.254,localhost,10.0.0.0/8,10.12.0.0/16"
ExecStart=/usr/bin/redwood-installer --offline
```

Jia (security): Small note: KMS/HSM outbound traffic typically doesn't go through the HTTP proxy (PKCS#11/tls sessions). Customers either need explicit allow rules to the HSM IP/CIDR or a private/peered network path. Add a short diagram or bullet list in the docs for that.

Maya (docs): Good call. I'll add a short subsection: "When proxying does not cover HSM/KMS" with allowed ports and example firewall rules.

Liam (infra): Also paste the nftables/iptables example we recommend for SNAT + conntrack. Keep it minimal, point out to adapt interface/IP.

Samir (eng): Here's the minimal nftables snippet we use in on-prem installs:
```nft
table ip nat {
  chain postrouting {
    type nat hook postrouting priority 100;
    oifname "eth0" snat to 54.12.34.56
  }
}
```
Note: replace oifname and IP, and include a conntrack accept rule if you need stateful allowances.

Liam (infra): Also add a short migration note: do not mix iptables-legacy and nftables shims. On some distro versions the iptables-nft compatibility layer can mask that rules are not applying. Recommend native nft where possible and include a link to our migration checklist.

Jia (security): Wording nit: prefer "allow list" instead of "allowlist" in customer-facing docs for clarity. Also include reminders about audit logging when customers open firewall to KMS endpoints.

Maya (docs): I'll open the PR with the snippets + checklist. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1428 (work in progress). I added troubleshooting steps: verify HTTP(S)_PROXY env, check NO_PROXY entries, validate route table for private subnets.

Jia (security): I'll review for the HSM wording and confirm port numbers (usually 1792/1793 for vendor; will paste exact list). :+1:

Maya (docs): Thanks all — will ping when PR is ready for final review. :rocket:
